question: Prediction of conversion from MCI to AD among ADNI MCI patients, both Alzheimer's-spectrum MCI. P-229's secondary experiment uses 393 ADNI MCI with conversion within 36 months; P-178 uses early MCI with conversion by the last visit (open horizon, mean 5.02 years). The shared channel is structural MRI. P-229 uses grey-matter volumes in 90 AAL regions only. P-178's 9-feature random forest includes hippocampal and ventricular volumes (its second- and third-ranked features) with cognitive scores, APOE4, age and race. Cohort subset, horizon and predictor set differ, which the rule allows. The record's P-229 figure (71.05%) is the SCD-to-MCI accuracy on the CLAS cohort, a misreading. The figures judged here are P-229's printed MCI-conversion results (Table IV, PDF page 30). The round-20 text extract stops at page 12 of 31 and does not contain them.
metric: ROC AUC with ROC AUC. Accuracy is not comparable here: converter prevalence is 12.8% in P-178 against 42.5% in P-229, and P-178's SVC reaches 0.900 accuracy by predicting the majority class (recall 1, AUC 0.52-0.55).

figures.P-229: IADT, pMCI vs sMCI on 393 ADNI MCI (167/226): AUC 0.7570, ACC 73.54%, SEN 69.46%, SPE 76.55%. These are consistent with 116/167, 173/226 and 289/393. The classifier is trained on labelled ADNI AD/NC with the MCI subjects unlabelled, and evaluated on all 393. Hanley-McNeil with 167/226: Q1 = 0.6090, Q2 = 0.6523, SE 0.0252, CI [0.708, 0.806]. The accuracy's Wilson CI is [0.690, 0.777].
figures.P-178: 9-feature RF: AUC 0.96, accuracy 0.936, on 95 held-out patients (about 12 converters/83 non-converters at the 12.8% rate). No interval is printed. Hanley-McNeil with 12/83: Q1 = 0.9231, Q2 = 0.9404, SE 0.040, CI [0.882, 1.000]. With all 49/334: SE 0.0197, CI [0.921, 0.999]. The 6-feature model without MRI volumes or APOE4 has AUC 0.88 (CI [0.751, 1.000] at 12/83).

matched_figure_check: No matched figure exists. P-178 reports no MRI-only model: its only reduced model drops the MRI volumes and APOE4 and keeps cognitive scores and demographics (AUC 0.88). It also reports no 36-month horizon and no all-MCI analysis. P-229 reports no cognitive or clinical predictors and no early-MCI or open-horizon analysis. Nothing in either paper reproduces the other's condition, so the gap is not reconciled. This is the same position as C-103 (P-178 against the MRI-only P-185), judged 'yes'.
performance_validity: Passes by the letter. P-178's 0.96 is below 0.97, though its test set is small (95 patients, about 12 converters) and it has no external cohort. P-229's 0.757 is far below. P-178's test-set composition is reported inconsistently (see the explanations).

candidate_explanations.difference: Predictor set: P-178 adds cognitive and functional scores (ADAS13, ADAS11, FAQ, MMSE), APOE4, age and race to two MRI volumes. P-229 uses MRI grey-matter volumes alone. P-178's model without the MRI volumes and APOE4 still reaches AUC 0.88, which points to the cognitive scores, but it is not an MRI-only comparison and so does not show the explanation is sufficient.
candidate_explanations.quote: We also tested a 6-feature group, which removed the RAVLT variables as well as the biomarker data; however, this saw the worst accuracy of the three groups at 89.2%.

candidate_explanations.difference: Label and horizon: conversion by the last available visit (mean time to conversion 5.02 years, up to 12 years in study) against conversion within 36 months.
candidate_explanations.quote: From the ADNI variables, the Clinical Dementia Rating was used to make this determination based on the value of their last visit's diagnosis.

candidate_explanations.difference: Training design: P-229's classifier never sees MCI conversion labels. It is trained on labelled AD/NC with the MCI subjects as an unlabelled target domain. P-178 trains directly on EMCI converter labels.
candidate_explanations.quote: A total of 393 MCI subjects (167 pMCI, 226 sMCI) with structural MRIs are used as the unlabeled target domain, while AD and NC samples are adopted as the labeled source domain.

candidate_explanations.difference: Population: early MCI only in P-178, against unselected ADNI MCI in P-229.
candidate_explanations.quote: 383 Early Mild Cognitive Impairment (EMCI) patients were gathered from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI). Of these patients, 49 would eventually convert to AD (EMCI_C), whereas the remaining 334 did not convert (EMCI_NC).

candidate_explanations.difference: Unit of analysis and a reporting inconsistency: P-178 works with visit records and oversampling. Table 1 lists an oversampled test set of 402 per class, but its SVC's 0.900 accuracy with recall 1 implies a test set about 90% one class. So what the 0.96 was computed over is unclear.
candidate_explanations.quote: This allows for the model to be trained against 2412 exam visits (1206 per class) rather than only the 1354 from the original data set train/test split.

reason: Both papers predict MCI-to-AD conversion in ADNI MCI with a model that includes structural MRI, and both report AUC. P-178's 0.96 (subject-level interval about 0.88-1.00) and P-229's printed MCI-conversion AUC 0.757 (0.708-0.806) lie outside each other's intervals, and neither paper reports a figure under the other's condition. The record's 71.05% for P-229 is its SCD task and was set aside under condition 6. On the figures the papers print, the gap may come from P-178's cognitive predictors, open horizon, early-MCI population, visit-level evaluation, or P-229's label-free transfer design, but neither paper shows any of these to be sufficient.

quotes.quote: The pMCI subjects have converted to AD within 36 months while sMCI have not. We still extract ROI features to represent each subject.
TABLE IV: Performance (%) of seven methods for MCI-to-AD conversion prediction (i.e., pMCI vs. sMCI classification). ... IADT (Ours) 73.54 73.00 75.70 69.46 76.55
our model achieves higher accuracy, balanced accuracy (i.e., 71.05%, 69.87%) and specificity (i.e., 73.08%) which are much better than the other three state-of-the-art methods
These pSCD subjects have evolved to MCI within the next 84 months, while the sSCD ones remain stable.
All of these patients were split randomly into training and testing data sets with 95 patients reserved for testing.
